chief_complaint: A 7-day history of fever, chills, headache and a dry cough.
history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with 7 days of fever, chills, headache and a dry cough. He had recently developed slide-positive falciparum malaria whilst living in southern Laos and was treated with intramuscular artemether 80 mg for 5 days, which he had brought from China as standby therapy. He did not improve; the fever persisted, and jaundice developed, leading to his transfer to a hospital in Vientiane.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is a Chinese itinerant trader who was living in southern Laos, where he contracted falciparum malaria. The case notes that artemisinin-resistant falciparum malaria has been described from southern Laos.
vitals: On admission, he was febrile with a temperature of 39.5°C (103.1°F). His blood pressure and Glasgow Coma Score were normal.
physical_exam: On admission, the patient had nausea, dry cough, moderate dehydration, chest pain and abdominal tenderness. His chest was clear on auscultation and no hepatosplenomegaly was detected.
labs_and_diagnostics: A Giemsa smear on admission was negative for malaria parasites, but a rapid diagnostic test (HRP-2) was positive for Plasmodium falciparum, consistent with recent infection. Serum creatinine and glucose were normal. Laboratory results showed elevated direct bilirubin at 6.4 µmol/L (reference <4.3 µmol/L) and elevated liver transaminases (ALT, AST).
differential_diagnosis: The differential diagnoses included bacterial coinfection with falciparum malaria, especially with Salmonella species. Other common infectious diseases in Laos such as scrub typhus, murine typhus, leptospirosis, tuberculosis, or dengue fever were also considered. The possibility of artemisinin-resistant falciparum malaria, incorrect dosing, poor drug quality, or issues with intestinal absorption of the artemether were also raised.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was treated with oral quinine sulphate 10 mg/kg every 8 hours and doxycycline 100 mg every 12 hours for 7 days. His fever cleared 35 hours after starting this therapy, and he was discharged well. No evidence was found for any other infections. Subsequent analysis of the artemether vial he used, via high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) and mass spectrometry (MS), demonstrated it was substandard and only contained 59 mg of artemether, which is 74% of the stated amount.
final_diagnosis: The final diagnosis was treatment failure of falciparum malaria due to the use of a substandard medication. The diagnosis was based on the patient's persistent fever after a course of artemether, a positive HRP-2 test for Plasmodium falciparum, and a rapid clinical response to a standard course of quinine and doxycycline. The cause was confirmed by chemical analysis showing the artemether he used was subtherapeutic, containing only 74% of the stated active ingredient, which resulted in underdosing.
